correctness.rationale: 2-connected outerplanar graphs are exactly polygons with noncrossing chord sets up to dihedral symmetries, because their Hamiltonian outer-face cycle is unique. The exhaustive binary recursion generates each legal chord set, and canonicalizing under all dihedral maps yields one representative per isomorphism type. Exact sorted refinement keys computed on the disjoint union and iterated to stabilization group graphs by their full 1-WL color histograms, with no stochastic hashing. The included standard-library certificate exhausts all such graphs for n=3,...,10 (up to 20793 chord sets/1117 graph types), identifies precisely five distinct doubletons at n=10 and zero earlier, and separately checks each pair. The proof states the finite bound and does not generalize beyond n=10.

value.rationale: The least size of an indistinguishable pair for ordinary 1-WL in the natural biconnected outerplanar graph class is a structurally significant threshold, motivated by a recent result showing that individualizing one vertex restores identification. The exhaustive enumeration classifies all boundary-order ambiguities and quantifies the precise gap between graph types and 1-WL classes, distinguishing a complete natural census from a routine recount of already-known isomorphism types or a single known counterexample. The sharp cutoff and all five pairs can inform tests of graph isomorphism heuristics and expressivity on outerplanar graphs.
